title: Legislative districts of Mountain Province
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Mountain Province''' are the representations of [[Mountain Province]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. The present-day [[Provinces of the Philippines|provinces]] of [[Apayao]], [[Benguet]], [[Ifugao (province)|Ifugao]] and [[Kalinga (province)|Kalinga]], as well as the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[Baguio]], formed part of the old (pre-division) Mountain Province's representation until 1969. Since 1969, the representation of Mountain Province has been confined only to the limits of the former sub-province of Bontoc. == History == === As the undivided Mountain Province (1908–1966) === Initially being excluded from representation in the [[Philippine Assembly|lower house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] in 1907, the then non-Christian-majority areas of the Philippines — which included the undivided [[Mountain Province]] — were finally extended legislative representation with the passage of the [[Jones Law (Philippines)|Philippine Autonomy Act]] in 1916 by the [[United States Congress]]. The Revised Administrative Code (Act No. 2711) enacted on March 10, 1917, further elaborated on the manner by which these areas would be represented.{{cite book|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Revised Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands of 1917 (Act No. 2711)|date=1917|publisher=Bureau of Printing|url=https://archive.org/stream/RevisedAdministrativeCodeOfThePhilippineIslandsOf1917/Revised%20Administrative%20Code%20of%20the%20Philippine%20Islands%20of%201917#page/n43/mode/2up|access-date=February 4, 2017|format=Digitized Revised Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands of 1917 from the Presidential Museum and Library Collection, uploaded on February 15, 2016}} The non-Christian areas were to be collectively represented in the [[Philippine Senate|upper house]]'s [[Philippines's 12th senatorial district|12th senatorial district]] by two senators, both appointed by the [[Governor-General of the Philippines|Governor-General]]. Three assembly members, also appointed by the Governor-General, were to represent the [[Mountain Province]] and the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|chartered city]] of [[Baguio]] in the [[Philippine Assembly|lower house]] as a [[#At-Large (defunct)|single at-large district]]. The appointment of these members of the Legislature did not require the consent of the upper house; the appointive legislators were also not necessarily required to be residents of the areas they represented.{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/stream/cu31924023544996#page/n59/mode/2up|page=57|publisher=Philippine Education Company, Inc.|year=1917 |title=Philippine Government|last=Cain|first=Andrew W.}} For example, [[#At-Large (defunct)|Assemblyman]] Pedro Aunario, a resident of [[Manila]],{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/stream/cu31924023544996#page/n159/mode/2up|page=157|publisher=Philippine Education Company, Inc.|year=1917|title=Philippine Government|last=Cain|first=Andrew W.}} and Senator [[Lope K. Santos]], a resident of [[Rizal (province)|Rizal]], were among the representatives of the Mountain Province. Despite several of the Mountain Province's municipalities and municipal districts being annexed to the neighboring provinces of [[Ilocos Sur]] (in 1920), [[La Union]] (in 1920) and [[Cagayan]] (in 1922 and 1928), voters in these areas were still represented by the [[#1917–1935|three assembly members of the Mountain Province]], and [[Philippines's 12th senatorial district|two senators of the twelfth senatorial district]]. Only starting in [[1935 Philippine legislative election|1935]] were these voters extended the right to participate in electing representatives of their respective new provinces, when Act No. 4203 assigned them to specific districts for the purposes of electing members of the unicameral [[National Assembly of the Philippines]]. Act No. 4203 also abolished the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines|senatorial district system]] and made the Mountain Province's representation to the [[National Assembly of the Philippines|National Assembly]] elective through popular vote; the law divided the province into three districts with definite territorial composition.{{cite journal|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Public Laws Enacted by the Philippine Legislature, Acts No. 4203 to 4275|journal=Public Resolutions, Etc |series=Laws, etc |date=1937|publisher=Bureau of Printing Office|page=5|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.35112102880830;view=1up;seq=133}} The only sub-province which belonged to more than one district was Bontoc: the eastern portion consisting of the present-day municipalities of [[Barlig]], [[Bontoc, Mountain Province|Bontoc]], [[Paracelis]], [[Natonin]], [[Sabangan]], [[Sadanga]] and [[Sagada]] were represented as part of the undivided province's [[#1st District (defunct)|first district]], while the western portion which formerly belonged to the now-defunct Lepanto sub-province ([[Bauko]], [[Besao]] and [[Tadian]]) were represented as part of the [[#3rd District (defunct)|third district]]. During the [[Second World War]], the Mountain Province sent [[#At-Large (defunct)|two delegates]] to the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. [[Baguio]], being a chartered city, was [[Legislative district of Baguio#At-Large (defunct)|represented separately]] in this short-lived legislative body. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, district representation was restored to the pre-war setup: the sub-province of Bontoc remained split between the [[#1st District (defunct)|first]] and [[#3rd District (defunct)|third]] districts, and the independent city of [[Baguio]] remained part of the [[#2nd District (defunct)|second district]]. === As the reduced Mountain Province (1966–present) === The enactment of Republic Act No. 4695 on June 18, 1966, made the sub-province of Bontoc into a full-fledged province that retained the name "Mountain Province."{{cite web|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/47_republicacts.php?id=4699|date=June 18, 1966|access-date=February 4, 2017|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|author=Congress of the Philippines|title=Republic Act No. 4695 - An Act Creating the Provinces of Benguet, Mountain Province, Ifugao and Kalinga-Apayao}} Per Section 10 of R.A. 4695 the three incumbent representatives of pre-division Mountain Province continued to serve their respective districts until the end of the [[6th Congress of the Philippines|6th Congress]]. The new (post-division) [[Mountain Province]] began electing its [[#Lone District|lone representative]] in [[1969 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1969]]. The province was represented as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region I]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#1984–1986|one representative, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, Mountain Province constituted a [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]],{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} and elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == Lone District == {{main|Mountain Province's at-large congressional district}} *'''Population (2015)''': 154,590{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date=2015|title=Population of Population of Legislative Districts by Region, Province, and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2015|access-date=November 27, 2017}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
